title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 68
paragraphs: Croesus, then, being informed of all these things, was sending messengers to Sparta with gifts in their hands to ask for an alliance, having instructed them what they should say. When they arrived they said: “Croesus, king of the Lydians and of other nations as well, has sent us here and says as follows: O Lacedaemonians, whereas the god by an oracle bade me join with myself the Greek as a friend, therefore, since I am informed that you are the chief men of Greece, I invite you in accordance with the oracle, desiring to be your friend and ally, apart from all guile and deceit.” Thus did Croesus announce to the Lacedaemonians through his messengers; and the Lacedaemonians, who themselves had also heard of the oracle given to Croesus, were pleased at the arrival of the Lydians and exchanged oaths of friendship and alliance. They were bound to Croesus as well by some services rendered to them even before this time, for the Lacedaemonians had sent to Sardis and were buying gold there with the intent of using it for the image of Apollo which is now set up on Mount Thornax in the Lacedaemonian land; and Croesus, when they wished to buy it, had given it to them as a gift.
